base_instruction: You are a helpful party planning assistant. Help the user plan a housewarming buffet by tracking guests, their dietary needs, and food choices. When asked to evaluate specific dishes, check each one against every current guest's dietary constraints. Pay attention to guest list changes and any corrections to dietary information throughout the conversation.

state_queue.anchor: Hey, I'm throwing a housewarming party next Saturday and want to do a buffet spread. Can you help me figure out the food?

flow_info.value: Six guests confirmed: me, my sister Rachel, my college buddy Marcus, my coworker Priya, and my neighbors Tom and his wife Linda
Rachel was diagnosed with celiac disease two years ago
Marcus had a bad reaction to shrimp at a wedding last year, his throat swelled up and he needed an EpiPen
Tom has been managing type 2 diabetes for about five years now
Trying to keep it around $200 total for food, maybe do some homemade and some store-bought
Priya just texted me she got called into a work emergency, she can't make it anymore

Marcus just messaged me actually — he said it wasn't just the shrimp. His allergist told him after more testing that it's all shellfish AND finned fish. Apparently he reacted to a cod dish too last month. So yeah, no seafood of any kind for him
Oh also, my friend Nina is coming too. She just moved back to town. She grew up in Ahmedabad in a Jain family, still follows it pretty strictly
Planning to put the food out around 5pm, people will graze for a few hours

Here's what I'm thinking for the buffet: smoked salmon crostini, Caesar salad with croutons, vegetable spring rolls, garlic shrimp skewers, a cheese and fruit platter, and brownies for dessert. How does that look?

constraints.value: Cannot eat gluten — no wheat, barley, rye, or products containing them
constraints.surface_form: Rachel was diagnosed with celiac disease two years ago
inference_chain: Celiac disease → autoimmune reaction to gluten
Gluten → found in wheat, barley, rye
Must avoid all gluten-containing foods including bread, pasta, most croutons, standard baked goods

constraints.value: Cannot eat shellfish — allergic reaction requiring EpiPen
constraints.surface_form: Marcus had a bad reaction to shrimp at a wedding last year, his throat swelled up and he needed an EpiPen
inference_chain: Severe reaction to shrimp with throat swelling → anaphylactic shellfish allergy
Shellfish allergy → avoid shrimp, crab, lobster, etc.

constraints.value: Cannot eat any seafood — shellfish AND finned fish, confirmed by allergist
constraints.surface_form: Marcus just messaged me actually — he said it wasn't just the shrimp. His allergist told him after more testing that it's all shellfish AND finned fish. Apparently he reacted to a cod dish too last month. So yeah, no seafood of any kind for him
inference_chain: Allergist testing revealed broader fish allergy
Constraint UPGRADED: shellfish → all seafood (shellfish + finned fish)

constraints.value: Should avoid high-sugar foods and desserts, needs low-glycemic options
constraints.surface_form: Tom has been managing type 2 diabetes for about five years now
inference_chain: Type 2 diabetes → must manage blood sugar
Managing blood sugar → avoid high-sugar foods, especially concentrated sweets

constraints.surface_form: Priya grew up vegetarian, her whole family is

constraints.value: Strict Jain diet — no meat, no fish, no eggs, no root vegetables (onion, garlic, potatoes, carrots)
constraints.surface_form: She grew up in Ahmedabad in a Jain family, still follows it pretty strictly
inference_chain: Jain family from Ahmedabad, follows strictly → practicing Jain
Jain dietary practice → no meat, no fish, no eggs
Strict Jain → also no root vegetables (onion, garlic, potatoes, carrots)

hidden_state.value: You are planning a housewarming buffet. You will introduce your guest list with their backgrounds, then updates will come in: one guest drops out, one guest's allergy gets corrected to be broader than initially stated, and a new guest joins late with strict dietary needs. At the end you will present a specific menu and ask how it looks. You never hint that there are dietary problems — you genuinely think the menu sounds good.

You are a relaxed, upbeat host excited about your new place. You relay updates from friends casually and matter-of-factly. You never express frustration when plans change — it's all part of party planning. When presenting the menu at the end, you sound genuinely pleased with your choices.
hidden_state.description: Prevents emotion escalation and maintains natural host tone

aims.description: Hey, I'm throwing a housewarming party next Saturday and want to do a buffet spread. Can you help me figure out the food?

So I've got six people confirmed including me: my sister Rachel, my college buddy Marcus, my coworker Priya, and my neighbors Tom and his wife Linda. Rachel was diagnosed with celiac disease two years ago. Marcus had a bad reaction to shrimp at a wedding last year — his throat swelled up and he needed an EpiPen. And Tom has been managing type 2 diabetes for about five years now. Priya grew up vegetarian, her whole family is. Linda eats everything, she's easy.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the guest list and dietary constraints
aims.conversation_goal: BURST — 5 entities with 4 constraints in one dense turn

aims.description: I'm trying to keep it around $200 total for food. Thinking I'll do some homemade stuff and grab some things from the store. What kind of mix would you suggest?
aims.success_criteria: Agent provides budget-conscious suggestions mixing homemade and store-bought

aims.description: Priya just texted me she got called into a work emergency, she can't make it anymore. Bummer, but at least that's one less person to worry about food-wise
aims.success_criteria: Agent notes Priya is no longer attending and her vegetarian constraint is removed
aims.conversation_goal: Entity EXIT — Priya leaves, vegetarian constraint removed

aims.description: Marcus just messaged me actually — he said it wasn't just the shrimp. His allergist told him after more testing that it's all shellfish AND finned fish. Apparently he reacted to a cod dish too last month. So yeah, no seafood of any kind for him
aims.success_criteria: Agent updates Marcus's constraint from shellfish-only to all seafood
aims.conversation_goal: Constraint UPGRADE — Marcus shellfish allergy → all seafood allergy

aims.description: Oh also, my friend Nina is coming too. She just moved back to town. She grew up in Ahmedabad in a Jain family, still follows it pretty strictly. So that brings us back to six people
aims.success_criteria: Agent registers Nina as a new guest with Jain dietary restrictions

aims.description: I'm planning to put the food out around 5pm and let people graze for a few hours. Should I worry about anything sitting out that long, food safety wise?
aims.success_criteria: Agent gives food safety advice about buffet timing

aims.conversation_goal: Noise turn — on-topic but creates distance before probe

aims.description: Good to know. Do you think paper plates are fine or should I use real dishes? I just moved in so I don't have a ton of stuff yet

drift_config.drift_topic: paper plates vs real dishes for a housewarming

aims.description: Here's what I'm thinking for the buffet: smoked salmon crostini, Caesar salad with croutons, vegetable spring rolls, garlic shrimp skewers, a cheese and fruit platter, and brownies for dessert. How does that look?
aims.success_criteria: Agent identifies problems with each dish against current guest constraints
aims.conversation_goal: Per-item verification of 6 dishes against current constraint state

ground_truth.answer: Smoked salmon crostini has multiple problems: salmon is finned fish (Marcus's upgraded seafood allergy), crostini is bread/gluten (Rachel's celiac), and Nina (Jain) cannot eat it either (fish). Caesar salad with croutons: croutons contain gluten (Rachel's celiac), and if the dressing contains anchovies or the salad has garlic, Nina cannot eat it (Jain — no fish, no root vegetables including garlic). Vegetable spring rolls: likely fine for most, but if they contain garlic or onion, Nina cannot eat them (Jain — no root vegetables). Garlic shrimp skewers: shrimp is shellfish (Marcus's seafood allergy), garlic is a root vegetable (Nina's Jain restriction). Cheese and fruit platter: fine for everyone currently attending. Brownies: high sugar is problematic for Tom (diabetes).
required_elements: Smoked salmon crostini is problematic for Marcus because salmon is finned fish and his allergy was upgraded to all seafood
Smoked salmon crostini is problematic for Rachel because crostini contains gluten and she has celiac disease
Garlic shrimp skewers are problematic for Marcus because shrimp is shellfish and he cannot eat any seafood
Garlic shrimp skewers are problematic for Nina because garlic is a root vegetable forbidden in strict Jain diet
Caesar salad with croutons is problematic for Rachel because croutons contain gluten
Brownies are problematic for Tom because they are high-sugar and he has type 2 diabetes
Cheese and fruit platter is fine for everyone currently attending
forbidden_elements: Flagging any dish as problematic for Priya (she is no longer attending)
Saying Marcus can only not eat shellfish (his allergy was upgraded to all seafood including finned fish)
Flagging the vegetarian constraint as still active (Priya left and she was the only vegetarian — Nina is Jain which is stricter but different)
Saying smoked salmon is fine for Marcus (salmon is finned fish, his upgraded allergy covers this)
ground_truth.explanation: This scenario tests constraint UPGRADE tracking as its primary difficulty mechanism. Marcus initially has a shellfish allergy (shrimp reaction), which is later corrected to a full seafood allergy (shellfish + finned fish). The smoked salmon crostini is the key trap item: if the agent only remembers the original shellfish constraint, it would incorrectly mark salmon as safe. Additional complexity: (1) Rachel's celiac requires inferring gluten avoidance — crostini and croutons both contain gluten. (2) Nina joins late as a high-constraint Jain entity — strict Jain means no meat, fish, eggs, or root vegetables (garlic, onion). The garlic shrimp skewers fail on TWO axes for TWO different people (Marcus: shrimp=seafood; Nina: garlic=root vegetable). (3) Priya exits, removing the vegetarian constraint — no dish should be flagged for vegetarian concerns unless it independently violates another active constraint. (4) Tom's diabetes means high-sugar brownies are problematic. (5) Cheese and fruit platter is the clearly-safe item. The over-generalization trap: Marcus has a seafood allergy, NOT a general food allergy — cheese, fruit, vegetables are all fine for him.

mechanism: Constraint UPGRADE: an initial constraint is corrected to a broader one
